ops.entry: WHEN measuring base-versus-head equivalence of a refactor DO run each side whole-process through its own entry, and attribute any difference by swapping only the code over one fixed tree — a substituted or shared runner hides load-shape differences such as added import-traceback frames.
ops.why: Validate c2: a seam receipt that ran a pristine entry against perturbed trees concealed 4 added traceback lines; own-entry whole-process runs revealed it, and c3's fixed-tree code swap attributed a route-mode difference to data not code. Displaces old G-04, now redundant because DEC-255 runner receipts already force a full per-kind run.

ops.entry: WHEN the repository's CI runs gates the QA matrix omits DO enumerate CI's required steps at the reviewed tip, run or name each omitted one, and confirm any gate a dispatch names actually exists there — a green matrix is not CI-green, and a phantom gate gets cited as coverage.
ops.why: Dispatch named a CI consolidation gate that the workflow never had; reporting it as CI-run would have falsified coverage. Same situation as G-02, sharpened at equal length.

Resolved this feature: bash-write-guard's allow/deny for cp/redirect turns on a literal versus shell-variable target (literal allowed, $VAR blocked), which explains the earlier inconsistent sessions; recorded in repository G-13.

originals.original: WHEN a task's own `verify:` command exercises only one script of a required kind DO also run the standing per-kind test command directly — a task-local pass can coexist with the kind itself never having been shown green across its full bucket.

WHEN the repository's CI runs gates the QA matrix omits (audits, route checks) DO enumerate CI's required steps and run or name each omitted one at the reviewed tip — a green matrix is not CI-green, and drift only those gates catch ships past repeated matrix_ok rounds.

WHEN a write-guard's behavior toward Bash-tool `cp`/redirect into the scratchpad is unclear DO confirm it with a controlled repro first — one QA session saw it deny such writes, a later session saw it allow them, and the discrepancy was never isolated to a cause.

ops.entry: WHEN writing, copying or deleting under bash-write-guard DO use literal absolute target paths — a redirect, cp or rm target containing a shell variable is blocked even under /tmp or the feature's notes/; do temp cleanup inside a python driver and pipe rather than redirect in loops.
ops.why: Reconfirmed across validate c1-c3 for cp and rm, not only redirects; widens G-13 to the measured class at the same length.

ops.entry: WHEN calling check-integration-shards helpers directly to check a runner receipt DO copy the call shape from validate-digest.py's own call site — discover_expected returns a (paths, error) tuple, and a stale call yields a misleading wall of unexpected/omitted defects, not a real receipt defect.
ops.why: Every validate run checks receipts with these helpers; a stale 2-arg call produced a false defect wall this feature. Pointer to the living call site, not an inlined recipe.

originals.original: WHEN redirecting output under bash-write-guard DO use a literal absolute target path — a redirect whose target contains a shell variable (e.g. `> mut-$m.txt`) is blocked even under /tmp; pipe to grep inside mutant loops instead.
